newsitem.title: UK: Now Britain bans smaller handguns too.
newsitem.headline: Now Britain bans smaller handguns too.

text.p: Britain's parliament voted overwhelmingly on Wednesday to approve one of the world's toughest gun laws, extending an existing ban on pistols to include all guns below .22-inch calibre.

The 384-173 vote followed an earlier ban on larger-calibre pistols which was passed after an explosion of public outrage over a massacre of 16 children and their teacher by a lone gunman last year at Dunblane primary school in Scotland.
Ministers are aiming to have the bill on the statute book by the summer recess in July.
The larger-calibre pistols have already been banned from July 1 after parliament approved a 150-million-pound ($245-million) package to compensate owners.
"It will no longer be possible to practise hand gun sports on the mainland of Britain," Home Secretary (interior minister) Jack Straw told parliament.
"But I want to make it clear that this will not in any way stop Britain hosting either the Commonwealth Games or, at some stage in the future, the Olympic Games."
Gun owners are angered by the tougher anti-gun laws and claim they are being made scapegoats for the act of a crazed, lone gunman.
They will have until September to dispose of their weapons or face a jail sentence of up to 10 years.

Media reports have said target shooters would travel to France and Belgium to pursue their sport and that target ranges were being planned for the Isle of Man and the Channel Islands where the anti-gun laws will not apply.
